title: Regional pin phased gateways checklist
summary: Lightweight, phased enforcement checklist for region pin (tenant pinning) rollout across private deployments and hybrid fleets. Focused on operator checkpoints, measurable telemetry gates, rollback criteria, and customer communication templates.
content:
Purpose:
This doc is an operator-facing checklist for rolling out region pin enforcement in private/VPC deployments. It is intentionally pragmatic: gate-by-gate, what to measure, how to react, and minimal artefacts to gather for audits. Use alongside legal/compliance sign-off and the zone-commitment SLAs.

Context and goals:
- Problem: customers require that data for pinned tenants never leave specific territories (country/region). We need an automated enforcement path that avoids outages and provides auditable evidence.
- Goal: progressive rollout with observable regression detection and fast rollback. Ensure every stage has a clear owner and an evidence bundle.

Phases (high level):
1) DESIGN VALIDATION (internal)
   - Owner: eng-private-deployments + compliance liaison
   - Deliverables: region-pin manifest examples, mapping table (tenant -> region), compatibility matrix for model variants and infra zones.
   - Checklist:
     - Confirm mapping exists for top 20 tenants by QPS (sample CSV attached to ticket).
     - Confirm fallback model variants for regions where full capacity is not available.
     - Identify any cross-region dependencies (logging, billing, auth) and mark them RISK.

2) STAGING CANARY (small-scale, synthetic + limited real tenants)
   - Traffic target: synthetic load + 0.1–1% of production tenants (prefer tenants who consent to test).
   - Duration: 72 hours minimum for multiple diurnal cycles.
   - Gate metrics (pass conditions):
     - Pin routing success rate >= 99.9% (no requests routed outside pinned region).
     - Error rate delta vs baseline < 0.1% absolute or < 20% relative (whichever is smaller).
     - 95th perc latency increase < 15ms.
     - No data residency audit failures (see evidence collection below).
   - Operator tasks:
     - Enable telemetry tags: tenant_id, pin_region, routed_zone, model_variant, request_id.
     - Run synthetic KV/prefix-cache warmup to simulate cold/steady state.
     - Collect and store sample traces for 1% of requests (retain for audit).

3) CUSTOMER CANARY (real customers, opt-in)
   - Traffic target: up to 5% of tenant traffic, prioritized low-risk customers.
   - Duration: 7 days minimum.
   - Gate metrics (pass conditions):
     - No P0/P1 incidents attributable to pin enforcement.
     - User-visible latency degradation < 10% for pinned tenants.
     - No cross-region data egress observed in network flow logs for pinned tenants.
   - Communication: send dedicated slack channel and weekly digest to on-call + customer success for participating customers.

4) GRADUAL ENFORCEMENT (ramped to 50%)
   - Ramp schedule: 10% -> 25% -> 50% over 7–14 days depending on metrics.
   - Gate metrics per step: repeat customer canary gates; require sustained stability for 48 hours at each step.

5) FULL ENFORCEMENT (100% of pinned tenants)
   - Precondition: legal & compliance checklist signed, risk register updated.
   - Post-conditions: daily audit reports generated automatically; infra owners notified of retention and eviction policies.

Evidence collection (auditable bundle):
- Routing evidence: per-request routing log (timestamp, tenant_id, routed_region, node_id, model_variant).
- Network flows: aggregated flow logs for the tenant's control plane endpoints.
- Trace samples: 1% sampled traces storing full routing path and decision reason.
- Configuration snapshots: region-pin manifests and commit SHAs for config applied.
- Sign-offs: compliance attestation (name, date), ops owner confirmation.

Automated checks to run before promoting a gate:
- TTL check: no stale pin manifests older than 24h.
- Drift detector: compare active routing table vs desired mapping, alert if >0 mismatches.
- Capacity check: cluster capacity headroom >= 20% in target regions for 48h.

Rollback & mitigation playbook (fast paths):
- Soft rollback (preferred): flip tenant to compatible fallback variant (same-region compatible) and mark for requeue.
- Hard rollback: disable enforcement policy and fall back to prior routing behavior. Triggered if any P0 incident or if routing success < 99% for >30 minutes.
- Communication templates: define a single-sentence incident banner for customers + internal slack snippet (examples below).

Operator runbook snippet (on-call):
- Pager fires: examine routing success metric and regional capacity dashboards.
- Run quick query: list top 10 tenants by failed-pin-count in last 15m.
- If failures concentrated in a single region: escalate to infra-zone on-call, tag incident PD.
- If failures spread: initiate hard rollback and notify CS / Legal.

Example slack alert (short):
[ALERT] region-pin: elevated routing failures for region eu-west-2 (pin success 92%) — oncall @infra-zone and @eng-private-deployments, action: investigate routing table drift or capacity exhaustion.

Customer communication snippet (for canary participants):
"Hi <Customer>, we’ve enabled region pin enforcement for your tenant as part of a short canary. We will monitor performance closely. Expect occasional restarts if a fallback is used; we’ll notify you for any changes. Contact <CS rep> for questions"

Operational telemetry & dashboards (minimum):
- Per-tenant pin success ratio (1m, 5m, 1h windows).
- P99 and P95 latency for pinned vs unpinned requests.
- Cross-region egress indicator (boolean + rate).
- Capacity headroom heatmap by region and GPU type.

Security/compliance notes:
- Ensure KMS keys for pinned tenants are region-bound where applicable.
- Ensure logs retained match audit retention policy; redact PII before shipping to central analytics if required.
- Record compliance attestation in evidence bundle after each enforcement milestone.

Open questions & decisions to surface:
- What is the canonical TTL for pin manifests? (current proposal: 24h, need legal buy-in)
- How do we treat transient cache misses that route to non-pinned warm nodes? (proposal: record as routed_outside, but do not count as hard failure if model_variant fallback used)
- SLA alignment: do we offer different latency/availability SLAs for pinned tenants that limit geo options?

Migration notes (when moving existing tenants):
- Run mapping audit: export existing tenant mapping and reconcile with desired region list.
- Schedule migration maintenance window for high-volume tenants (>10x average).
- Provide customers a pre-migration report: expected latency delta, available model variants, and potential downgrade of throughput during move.

Appendix: quick checklist for gate-owners (copyable)
- [ ] Review mapping for gate cohort (owner: product)
- [ ] Confirm telemetry tags are enabled for cohort (owner: infra)
- [ ] Run synthetic warmup for target regions (owner: serving-runtime)
- [ ] Validate no legal holds or export constraints (owner: compliance)
- [ ] Execute canary and collect evidence bundle (owner: ops)
- [ ] Sign off to promote to next gate (owner: gate steward)

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add template scripts for evidence bundle export (s3 path pattern + retention)
- Wire up an automated slack notification when drift detector fires
- Draft legal FAQ for customers regarding pin tradeoffs

References and links (tickets to follow up):
- PD-842: region pin rollout epic
